GDNF is expressed in the adult midbrain dopaminergenic system, and its levels are higher in the ventromedial than in the dorsolateral striatum, and that GDNF is a neuroprotectant of ventromedial dopaminergenic cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the striatal GDNF expression in the differential vulnerability between midbrain dopaminergics neurons.
the neuroprotective role of endogenous GDNF in the adult brain.
the role of endogenous GDNF as a physiological neurotrophic factor for midbrain DA cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

GDNF, which is constitutively expressed by striatal cells and by DA neurons projecting to the ventral striatal region, plays a neuroprotectant role against 6‐OH‐induced degeneration of DA neurons in the midbrain.
the striatum expresses GDNF that is transported back to the midbrain and acts as a trophic factor for midbrain DA neurons.

GDNF is a trophic factor for DA cells, which is constitutively expressed and released in the striatum, where it acts as an autocrine and/or paracrine factor, and is expressed in the DA cell bodies in the midbrain where it acts as a neuroprotective agent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GDNF, expressed in the vSt, is retrogradely transported by VTA and SNm DA cells and that it plays a neuroprotecting role in the mesostriatal dopaminergic system.
GDNF expressed in the striatum may act in a paracrine fashion to protect midbrain DA neurons.
GDNF, which has been considered a trophic factor only when exogenously administered, also plays an endogenous neuroprotective role in adult brain.
The main takeaway from our work is that

GDNF expression by striatal target cells may be a physiological factor involved in the resistance of midbrain DA cells to neurodegenerative insults, such as 6‐OH‐D, and may contribute to the neuroprotective effect of GDNF in the treatment of Parkinson's disease.
GDNF expression in the adult brain may play a physiological role in the protection of midbrain DA cells, and that this effect is mediated by the striatum, the target region of midbrain DA axons.
GDNF is not a mere trophic factor but also a neuromodulator of the adult mesostiratal system.
